newsitem.title: UK: S&P says may cut Northern Electric ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P says may cut Northern Electric ratings.

text.p: Standard and Poor's said on Monday it had placed the A senior unsecured and A1 commercial paper ratings of Northern Electric Plc on CreditWatch with negative implications.
"A total of 200 million sterling ($302 million) of debt is affected," S&P said.
It said the CreditWatch placement followed the announcement of a takeover bid for Northern by CE Electric U.K., valuing the U.K. regional electricity company at 651 million sterling
"CE Electric is 70 percent-owned by U.S. project company CalEnergy (rated BB with a stable outlook)," S&P said.

"The CreditWatch rating action acknowledges uncertainties concerning the future credit quality of Northern Electric, should the bid by CE Electric succeed, any takeover defence measures implemented by Northern and any actions of the U.K. Office of Electricity Regulation (OFFER) in response to the proposed takeover," S&P said.

It is a general rating criterion of Standard & Poor's that a subsidiary be rated no higher than its parent. An exception may be made where there is clear, specific, and compelling evidence that regulatory protection would limit subsidiary bondholder exposure to the parental credit quality.
S&P said that to date, it had taken the view that the regulatory "ring-fencing" established by OFFER did not provide material protection for utility bondholders.
"Accordingly, a successful acquisition of Northern by CE Electric could result in a rating equal to that of its ultimate parent CalEnergy, currently rated BB," it said.

"In assessing the impact of a successful CalEnergy acquisition of Northern, S&P will take into account any further actions by the regulator that would clarify the degree to which Northern bondholders may be insulated from parent company credit risk," Standard & Poor's said.
